sowing_window: Late April to Early June (North India); May to June (Central & South India)
soil_requirement: Deep black soils (Regur) or medium-heavy soils with good drainage; pH 6.0 to 8.0.
seed_rate: Bt Cotton: 1.5 to 2.0 kg per acre; Non-Bt: 4 to 5 kg per acre.
spacing: 90 cm x 60 cm or 120 cm x 45 cm depending on soil fertility and plant vigor.
key_advisory: Avoid sowing after late June to prevent peak pink bollworm infestation matching flowering. Treat seeds with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg seed or Imidacloprid 70WS @ 5g/kg for sucking pest protection during the first 30 days.
source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Annual Package of Practices

sowing_window: Mid-March to Mid-May (Olitorius / Tossa jute: Mid-April to May; Capsularis / White jute: March to April)
soil_requirement: Rich alluvial, sandy-loam or clay-loam soils along river basins; tolerates mild acidity (pH 5.5 to 7.0).
seed_rate: Line sowing: 5 to 6 kg/ha (Tossa) or 7 to 8 kg/ha (White); Broadcasting: 8 to 10 kg/ha.
spacing: 25 cm to 30 cm line spacing, thinned to 7 to 10 cm between plants at 3 weeks.
key_advisory: Ensure pre-sowing soil moisture. Capsularis varieties (e.g. JRC-321, JRC-212) resist waterlogging in low-lying areas. Olitorius varieties (JRO-524, JRO-204) yield finer fiber but need upland well-drained soils. Sowing past late May severely reduces fiber tensile strength.
source: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres (CRIJAF)

sowing_window: Kharif: June to July nursery, July to August transplanting; Rabi: October to November nursery, November to December transplanting; Summer: January to February nursery.
soil_requirement: Well-drained sandy loam or clay loam rich in organic matter; pH 6.0 to 7.0; sensitive to waterlogging.
seed_rate: Hybrids: 100 to 150 grams per acre; Open-pollinated: 200 to 250 grams per acre.
spacing: Transplant 25 to 30 day old seedlings at 60 cm x 45 cm (determinate) or 90 cm x 45 cm (indeterminate staked).
key_advisory: Solarize nursery beds or drench with Trichoderma harzianum to avoid damping-off. For Kharif planting, use virus-resistant hybrids (e.g. Arka Rakshak, Arka Samrat) capable of resisting Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV).

sowing_window: Timely sown irrigated: 1st to 20th November; Late sown: Up to 25th December.
soil_requirement: Well-drained fertile clay loams or loamy soils; optimum pH 6.5 to 7.5.
seed_rate: Timely sown: 100 kg/ha (40 kg/acre); Late sown or bold grains: 125 kg/ha.
spacing: 20 cm to 22.5 cm row-to-row spacing; depth of 4 to 5 cm.
key_advisory: Delaying sowing beyond 20th November leads to a yield penalty of 35-40 kg per hectare per day due to terminal heat stress during grain filling in March. Use recommended varieties like HD-2967, PBW-550, or DBW-187 (Karan Vandana).
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR)

sowing_window: Kharif nursery: May to June, transplanting July; Boro/Rabi nursery: November to December, transplanting January.
soil_requirement: Heavy clay soils with low water permeability and high moisture retention capacity; pH 5.5 to 7.5.
seed_rate: Transplanted: 15 to 20 kg/acre for varieties, 6 to 8 kg/acre for hybrids; Direct Seeded (DSR): 8 to 10 kg/acre.
spacing: 20 cm x 15 cm with 2-3 seedlings per hill, planted 2 to 3 cm deep.
key_advisory: In North-West plains (Punjab/Haryana), adhere strictly to notified nursery sowing dates (after May 20) and transplanting (after June 15-20) to conserve groundwater under State Water Preservation Acts.

sowing_window: Late September to late October (Ideal: October 10 to October 25)
soil_requirement: Sandy loam to light loam with good drainage; pH 6.0 to 7.5.
spacing: 45 cm row spacing, 10-15 cm plant spacing; depth 3 to 4 cm.
key_advisory: Ensure optimum soil moisture at sowing. Early sowing in mid-October escapes peak aphid infestation during flowering and pod development.

sowing_window: Mid-October to Mid-November (Rainfed: First fortnight of October; Irrigated: Late October to early November)
soil_requirement: Deep, well-drained medium to heavy soils; avoid saline and alkaline soils.
seed_rate: Desi varieties: 65 to 75 kg/ha; Kabuli bold seeded: 100 to 120 kg/ha.
spacing: 30 cm x 10 cm; depth 7 to 10 cm to utilize subsoil moisture.
key_advisory: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium and PSB culture @ 50g each per kg seed. Deep sowing protects young seedlings from Fusarium wilt and collar rot.

sowing_window: Kharif nursery: May to June; Late Kharif: August to September; Rabi nursery: October to November (transplanting Dec-Jan).
soil_requirement: Friable, fertile sandy loam to clay loam soils with high organic matter; pH 6.5 to 7.5.
seed_rate: 3 to 4 kg per acre for nursery raising.
spacing: 15 cm x 10 cm on flat or raised beds.
key_advisory: Rabi crop produces highest yield and storage quality. Avoid excess nitrogen after bulb enlargement to prevent neck rot and bolting.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR)
